items.item:
12. An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and
    pointers, the Customers it made, one closure holding the file's digest and
    exactly one audit entry; a failure inside its transaction leaves none of
    them — no project, room, pointer, Customer, closure or entry.
   Shows A16-1. [witness: verification:registry_a16_accepted_import_stores_all_in_one_transaction]
statements:
```text
import(file f, picks P) accepted => stored(P with rooms, pointers) and
stored(new customers of P) and closure.file_digest = digest(f) and one
AuditEntry, in one transaction   -- A16-1
exists closure => import refused   -- A16-2
mapping(f, P) shows a conflict or a malformed record => no confirmation step
for P, import(f, P) not accepted, store unchanged   -- A16-3
```

for table in IMPORTED_TABLES:
        assert rt.store_rows(table) == [], table

assert sorted(r["project_id"] for r in rt.store_rows("project_rows")) == [
        "v1-p1",
        "v1-p2",
    ]

assert sorted(r["room_id"] for r in rt.store_rows("room_rows")) == [
        "v1-r1",
        "v1-r2",
        "v1-r3",
    ]

assert sorted(r["pointer_id"] for r in rt.store_rows("pointer_rows")) == [
        "v1-e1",
        "v1-e2",
    ]
verdicts.why: The check verifies the exact picked projects, rooms, pointers, and created Customer, and tuple-unpacks the closure and audit tables to require exactly one row while checking the closure digest. It injects a failure at the final audit-entry write and verifies the complete store snapshot is restored and every imported table and Customer listing remains empty, thereby detecting a split or non-atomic transaction.
